claims.claim: Origen of Alexandria was a Christian theologian and head of the Catechetical School of Alexandria who lived approximately from 185 to 254 CE.
Origen’s Commentary on Lamentations was composed in the early 220s, most likely between 222 and 225 CE, making it one of his earliest biblical commentaries.

The work was written as a literal, grammatical exposition of the Book of Lamentations, establishing the Hebrew form of the text, its historical background, and comparing the various Greek translations.
The original commentary has been lost; its fragments survive only in Byzantine catenae (chains) that quoted short passages from older exegetical works.
The preserved fragments show Origen’s method of treating Scripture as a grammateus, a scholar who first determines the literal sense before moving to higher theological meanings.
